message.content:
The title of “best player” in soccer is always debated and depends on the criteria you use—goals, assists, influence on the game, trophies, or overall skill. As of now, a few names frequently come up:

| Player | Club | Position | Why they’re often mentioned |
|--------|------|----------|-----------------------------|
| **Lionel Messi** | Inter Miami (MLS) | Forward | Still producing goals and assists, and his play‑making remains top‑class. |
| **Kylian Mbappé** | Paris Saint‑Germain | Forward | Explosive pace, finishing, and a key player for France. |
| **Erling Haaland** | Manchester City | Striker | Record‑breaking goal‑scoring rate in the Premier League and Champions League. |
| **Kevin De Bruyne** | Manchester City | Midfielder | One of the best passers and play‑makers in the world. |
| **Neymar Jr.** | Al‑Hilal (Saudi Pro League) | Forward | Still a creative force and a global icon. |

If you’re looking at pure statistics for the current season, **Erling Haaland** has been the most prolific scorer in Europe, while **Kevin De Bruyne** consistently tops the assist charts. In terms of overall influence and versatility, many analysts still point to **Lionel Messi** as the most complete player, even though he’s moved to MLS.

Ultimately, the “best” player can vary depending on whether you value individual brilliance, team success, or a combination of both.
